newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to double some tea import taxes from June 1.
newsitem.headline: Russia to double some tea import taxes from June 1.

text.p: Russia will double duties on some tea imports from June 1, a State Customs Committee spokesman said on Tuesday, quoting a government decree.
Under the decree, a 20 percent import tax will be payable on green, non-fermented tea and on black, fermented and partly-fermented tea arriving in packages of less than three kilos each.
The new tax would be introduced on June 1 and doubles the current 10 percent levy, the spokesman said.

The new measures include a new, higher minimum import levy of 0.4 Ecus per kg for both categories of tea, up from the previous minimum of 0.1 Ecus, according to the decree, which was signed last month.
The committee implements government-ordered changes to the import system.

Russian tea industry sources said that some major tea exporters to Russia, including India and Sri Lanka, would pay only 15 percent import duties under the new tax regime because they belonged to the General System of Preferences (GSP).
This allows them to pay only 75 percent of the duties.

The higher import tax is in addition to a 20 percent value-added tax (VAT) paid on all imported tea. VAT is paid on the landed cost of the tea in Russia, and therefore includes import tax costs, the sources said.
They also said another 1.5 percent is paid in taxes on all goods imported to Russia.

Russia is a major tea importer, with deliveries reaching 147,491 tonnes in 1995, the last year for which figures were available. This was up sharply on the 91,759 tonnes imported in 1994. India is by far its biggest supplier.
